### Summary

I am using st.file_uploader to upload ~3.5gb file into my streamlit dashboard. This however, results in the server getting killed.
When I inspect using btop, Upon file upload, the server starts using an astronomic amount of RAM.

EDIT: I tried imposing a RAM limit by dockerizing the dashboard and settting a 4gb RAM limit, but it just gets killed in the container.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a video file", type=["mp4", "mov", "avi"])
```


### Steps To Reproduce

streamlit run dashboard.py --maxUploadSize=5000

### Expected Behavior

It's probably better to stream it in chunks to disk when clicking an 'upload file' button.

### Current Behavior

The server gets killed.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Streamlit version:
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

facts_with_quotes.quote:
cache_data failing to serialize classes from v1.44.0

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I noticed in the upgrade from 1.43.0 to 1.44.0 that we are getting UnserializableReturnValueError when calling cache_data with a self defined class. I can confirm pickle dumps and loads works fine for this class when I run it outside of streamlit. 

Full error:
> streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type __main__.Example) in test(). st.cache_data uses pickle to serialize the function's return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see our docs for differences).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit import cache_data
import datetime as dt

class Example:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

@cache_data(ttl=dt.timedelta(minutes=60))
def test():
    name = "andy"
    return Example(name)

if __name__ == '__main__':

    b = test()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code above in streamlit

### Expected Behavior

The class should be pickled and be stored in the cache

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.44.0
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome

Application Crash: file_uploader kills streamlit when used in a page via st.navigation 1.47 and 1.48 at least

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi,

Platform is windows 11, recent python, streamlit version 1.47 and 1.48

I can't see this described in the issues list.

I just spend a couple of hours tracing a very strange problem with st.file_uploader. The problem affects files of any size, including 1kB and doesn't seem to cause run away memory usage in streamlit.

If I create a simple app with the following file_uploader everything works as expected, file is uploaded and the message is printed

```
  import streamlit as st
  
  st.write(st.__version__)
  
  uploads = st.file_uploader("Upload one or more files")
  
  if uploads is not None:
      st.write("uploads")

```
However, if I create an application like this. Then the upload proceeds for a few seconds and then the server process dies with no diagnostics.

app.py

```
import streamlit as st

pg = st.navigation([
    st.Page("Upload_Data.py", title="Upload data"),
])
pg.run()

```

Upload_Data.py

```
import streamlit as st

st.write(st.__version__)

uploads = st.file_uploader("Upload one or more files")

if uploads is not None:
    st.write("uploads")


```

If I replace the string with the python filename with a function, which does the same thing then the function works correctly.

Expected behaviour

Application doesn't crash when using file_uploader in pages loaded via st.navigation.

Thanks for your help and any pointers.

Mike

```Python

gc.collect()

summary.problem:
Add an option to fully disable sidebar rendering until authentication or page load is complete

Currently, Streamlit always renders the sidebar and multipage navigation menu before any backend logic runs.
This causes a brief flash (“flicker”) of the sidebar, even when developers try to hide it using CSS, st.set_page_config(initial_sidebar_state="collapsed"), or st.stop() during login checks.

Problem

When implementing authentication or loading processes (e.g., validating user credentials via an API), Streamlit renders the sidebar before the authentication state is known.
This behavior creates two key issues:

Security concern:
Unauthenticated users can briefly see and click sidebar navigation links before st.stop() halts the script, allowing them to access or attempt to load protected pages.
Even if no data is exposed, it creates a visible loophole and inconsistent behavior.

UX inconsistency:
The sidebar “flashes” for a fraction of a second during app load, even when the developer intends to display only a centered login screen or full-screen loading animation.
This leads to a jarring visual experience and makes professional deployments look less polished.

Why this matters

Many enterprise and production Streamlit apps use custom login systems, SSO integrations, or data validation APIs before showing any content.

In these cases, developers need full control over what renders before authentication completes.

There’s currently no reliable way to prevent the sidebar or multipage navigation from being rendered briefly.


Proposed solution

Add a configuration flag such as:
st.set_page_config(show_sidebar_on_load=False)

st.cache_data on class methods intermittently raises UnserializableReturnValueError

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
### `repro_model.py`


"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:
    def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0):
        self.output = output
        self.value = value


### `repro_agent.py`


"""
Helper module imported once by repro.py.
Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference
after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.
"""
import streamlit as st
from repro_model import MyResult  # bound once at import time


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    import time
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return MyResult(output=f"result for {key}", value=42)


### `repro.py` — run with `streamlit run repro.py`


import streamlit as st
import sys
import importlib
import repro_agent  # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py


st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro")

if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"):
    try:
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")

if st.button("2) Simulate file-watcher then call (fails, and keeps failing)"):
    # This is exactly what LocalSourcesWatcher.on_path_changed does:
    #   for wm in self._watched_modules.values():
    #       del sys.modules[wm.module_name]
    if "repro_model" in sys.modules:
        del sys.modules["repro_model"]

    # Re-import creates a NEW class object in sys.modules
    importlib.import_module("repro_model")

    # Clear cache so pickle.dumps is attempted again
    repro_agent.get_result.clear()

    try:
        # rep

st.cache_data shares cache across st.Page pages for same-named functions with different source code

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.cache_data functions with the same name but different source code in different page files (loaded via st.navigation + st.Page) share the same cache. This is because st.Page executes all pages via exec() with
  __module__ == "__main__", and inspect.getsource() fails in that context. The fallback to func.__code__.co_code (bytecode) does not include string constants, so functions with identical structure but different inline strings (e.g., different SQL queries) produce the same cache key.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# main.py
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(page_title="Cache Bug Demo", layout="wide")
pg = st.navigation(
    {
        "Page A": [st.Page("page_a.py", title="Page A")],
        "Page B": [st.Page("page_b.py", title="Page B")],
    }
)
pg.run()
# page_a.py
import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_a", "columns": ["col_a1", "col_a2"]}


data = load_data()
st.write("Page A data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_a, Got:", data["source"])
# page_b.py
import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_b", "columns": ["col_b1", "col_b2"]}


data = load_data()
st.write("Page B data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_b, Got:", data["source"])
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create the three files above (main.py, page_a.py, page_b.py)
2. Run streamlit run main.py
3. Open Page A — displays source: page_a (correct)
4. Navigate to Page B — displays source: page_a (wrong, should be page_b)
5. Clear cache and open Page B first — displays source: page_b (correct)
6. Navigate to Page A — displays source: page_b (wrong, should be page_a)

### Expected Behavior

Each page's load_data() should have an independent cache, since they are defined in different files with different source code. Navigating between pages should return each page's own data.

st.cache_data shares cache across st.Page pages for same-named functions with different source code

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.cache_data functions with the same name but different source code in different page files (loaded via st.navigation + st.Page) share the same cache. This is because st.Page executes all pages via exec() with
  __module__ == "__main__", and inspect.getsource() fails in that context. The fallback to func.__code__.co_code (bytecode) does not include string constants, so functions with identical structure but different inline strings (e.g., different SQL queries) produce the same cache key.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(page_title="Cache Bug Demo", layout="wide")
pg = st.navigation(
    {
        "Page A": [st.Page("page_a.py", title="Page A")],
        "Page B": [st.Page("page_b.py", title="Page B")],
    }
)
pg.run()
# page_a.py
import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_a", "columns": ["col_a1", "col_a2"]}


data = load_data()
st.write("Page A data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_a, Got:", data["source"])
# page_b.py
import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_b", "columns": ["col_b1", "col_b2"]}


data = load_data()
st.write("Page B data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_b, Got:", data["source"])
```

2. Run streamlit run main.py

5. Clear cache and open Page B first — displays source: page_b (correct)
6. Navigate to Page A — displays source: page_b (wrong, should be page_a)

### Summary

Hello everyone. 

In my use case, I have a multipage application, with an st.selectbox on top of every subpage. The default value of those selectboxes is taken from st.session_state. The bug I have encountered now is that when I want to update the selectbox value I need to select the new value twice. An example

Selected option: 1
I select option 2.
Selected option: 1
I select option 2 again.
Selected option: 2

From then on the value is updated and working as expected. This behavior is 100% reproducible for me but only happening after I updated the selected option once i.e. directly after the start of the application it works fine and expected once. Afterward I need to double select the options.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
app.py:
import streamlit as st

def main():
    pg = st.navigation([st.Page("page1.py")])
    pg.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()


page1.py:
import streamlit as st


def page():
    if "selectedIndex" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state["selectedIndex"] = 0
    
    selectedIndex = st.selectbox(
        label="Select something:", 
        options=range(0, 5),
        index=st.session_state["selectedIndex"]
    )
    
    st.session_state["selectedIndex"] = selectedIndex
    
    st.write(f"You selected {selectedIndex}.")
    st.write(f"Session state {st.session_state["selectedIndex"]}.")


page()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start the application `streamlit run app.py`
2. Update the select box value to 3.
4. Select option 1.
6. Select option 1 again.

You can repeat steps 4-7 as often as you want; it will happen every time.

### Expected Behavior

1. Start the application `streamlit run app.py`
2. Update the select box value to 3.
3. The value is now correctly set as 3.
4. Select option 1.6. 
5. The value is now correctly set as 1.

### Current Behavior

No error messages.

1. Start the application `streamlit run app.py`
2. Update the select box value to 3.
3. The value is now correctly set as 3.
4. Select option 1.
5. The selected value will jump back to 3. The return value and session state value also don't update.
6. Select option

summary.problem:
Deleting a widget's session_state key leaves the frontend showing the stale value (backend/frontend divergence for one rerun)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Deleting a keyed widget's entry from `st.session_state` (e.g. `del st.session_state["foo"]` inside a callback) does not reset the widget, but can lead to an inconsistency between frontend and backend.

The Python side returns the widget's *default* value for that run, but the frontend keeps displaying the old value, so backend and frontend disagree.

On the **next** rerun the backend silently re-adopts the stale frontend value, so the deletion is effectively undone.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

text = st.text_input("Foo", value="default", key="foo")

st.write("widget returned:", repr(text))

def populate():
    st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"

def delete():
    del st.session_state["foo"]

st.button("Populate", on_click=populate)
st.button("Delete", on_click=delete)
st.button("Noop")

```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app.
2. Click **Populate** (callback sets `st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"`). The text input now shows `hello` and `widget returned: 'hello'`.
3. Click **Delete** (callback runs `del st.session_state["foo"]`).
4. Observe the text input on screen vs. the `widget returned:` line.
5. Click **Noop** (any interaction that triggers a plain rerun) and observe again.

### Expected Behavior

The widget value in the frontent and backend should be consistent. After deleting a widget's key in session state, it should presumably fall back to its default value.

### Current Behavior

- After clicking Delete, the backend returns `widget returned: "default''` , but the frontend widget still displays `"hello"`.
- After the next rerun (step 5), the backend re-adopts the stale frontend value, and both show `"hello"`.

### Screenshot

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Python version: 3.14.6
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04
- Browser: Chromium

summary.problem:
`setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`

### Summary

When a Components V2 component calls `setTriggerValue` during mount (inside the default function, rather than from a user event handler), values are silently lost if the component remounts because its `data` changed — even when an explicit `key` is passed, which keeps the element id stable.

Measured roughly a quarter loss: **5 of 21 values sent were never received by Python at all.** They are not late — a scan of the entire session log shows they never arrive in any subsequent run.

This is split out of #14710, where it surfaced during investigation. It is distinct from the two by-design mechanisms discussed there (`data` participating in element identity for unkeyed components, and trigger values resetting after each run).

**Update — measured root cause.** A frontend race in `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive`: it destroys the synthetic trigger-aggregator widget state while that state is still awaiting its batched flush, so the app reruns with no trigger at all. Not a backend discard. Measured on a production build with the repro below: 10/85 values lost unpatched vs 0/85 patched, and with instrumentation, 14/14 losses correlated exactly with the destroying call. Mechanism and open question under Additional Information.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

comp = st.components.v2.component(
    "repro.mount_trigger",
    js="""
    export default function (component) {
        const v = "val" + component.data.nonce;
        console.log("SEND " + v);
        component.setTriggerValue("v", v);
    }
    """,
)

if "clicks" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.clicks = 0
if st.button("bump"):
    st.session_state.clicks += 1

nonce = f"c{st.session_state.clicks}"
result = comp(data={"nonce": nonce}, key="stable_key")

received = result.get("v")
st.write(f"data nonce {nonce} -> received {received!r}")
print(f"nonce={nonce} received={received!r}", flush=True)
```

1. Run the app and open the browser console.
2. Click **bump** ~20 times, letting the app settle between clicks. Each click changes `data`, so the component remounts and sends one value.
3. Compare the `SEND val…` lines in the console against the `received=…` lines in the terminal.
4. Roughly one in four sent values never appears on the Python side.

summary.problem:
Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for tha

facts_with_quotes.quote:
AppTest: synchronize query parameters when interacting with query-bound widgets

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Please make AppTest's widget interaction API synchronize query parameters for widgets using `bind="query-params"`. Currently, `.set_value(...).run()` changes the widget value but leaves both `at.query_params` and the app's `st.query_params` unchanged, so tests observe a different state from the browser.

### Why?

Native query-param binding lets apps replace manual URL callbacks. After that change, AppTest tests that verify shareable filters or inspect `st.query_params` can no longer reproduce the state reached by the same user interaction in the browser. Each test must manually mirror the binding's serialization into `at.query_params`.

The following self-contained example demonstrates the gap on Streamlit 1.65.0; it also occurs on 1.64.0:

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

st.selectbox("FC", ["A", "B"], key="fc", bind="query-params")
st.session_state["seen_query"] = dict(st.query_params)
""").run()

at.selectbox[0].set_value("B").run()
assert not at.exception
print("Widget:", at.selectbox[0].value)
print("AppTest query params:", at.query_params)
print("App query params:", at.session_state["seen_query"])
```

Save as `repro_query_binding.py` and run `python repro_query_binding.py` with `streamlit==1.65.0` installed. No pytest or app-specific dependencies are required.

Observed:

```text
Widget: B
AppTest query params: {}
App query params: {}
```

AppTest: synchronize query parameters when interacting with query-bound widgets

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Please make AppTest's widget interaction API synchronize query parameters for widgets using `bind="query-params"`. Currently, `.set_value(...).run()` changes the widget value but leaves both `at.query_params` and the app's `st.query_params` unchanged, so tests observe a different state from the browser.

### Why?

Native query-param binding lets apps replace manual URL callbacks. After that change, AppTest tests that verify shareable filters or inspect `st.query_params` can no longer reproduce the state reached by the same user interaction in the browser. Each test must manually mirror the binding's serialization into `at.query_params`.

The following self-contained example demonstrates the gap on Streamlit 1.65.0; it also occurs on 1.64.0:

```python

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

st.selectbox("FC", ["A", "B"], key="fc", bind="query-params")
st.session_state["seen_query"] = dict(st.query_params)
""").run()

at.selectbox[0].set_value("B").run()
assert not at.exception
print("Widget:", at.selectbox[0].value)
print("AppTest query params:", at.query_params)
print("App query params:", at.session_state["seen_query"])
```

AppTest query params: {}
App query params: {}

cache_data failing to serialize classes from v1.44.0

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I noticed in the upgrade from 1.43.0 to 1.44.0 that we are getting UnserializableReturnValueError when calling cache_data with a self defined class. I can confirm pickle dumps and loads works fine for this class when I run it outside of streamlit. 

Full error:
> streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type __main__.Example) in test(). st.cache_data uses pickle to serialize the function's return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see our docs for differences).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit import cache_data
import datetime as dt

class Example:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

@cache_data(ttl=dt.timedelta(minutes=60))
def test():
    name = "andy"
    return Example(name)

if __name__ == '__main__':

    b = test()
```

Run the code above in streamlit

The class should be pickled and be stored in the cache

summary.problem:
cache_data failing to serialize classes from v1.44.0

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I noticed in the upgrade from 1.43.0 to 1.44.0 that we are getting UnserializableReturnValueError when calling cache_data with a self defined class. I can confirm pickle dumps and loads works fine for this class when I run it outside of streamlit. 

Full error:
> streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type __main__.Example) in test(). st.cache_data uses pickle to serialize the function's return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see our docs for differences).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit import cache_data
import datetime as dt

class Example:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

@cache_data(ttl=dt.timedelta(minutes=60))
def test():
    name = "andy"
    return Example(name)

if __name__ == '__main__':

    b = test()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code above in streamlit

### Expected Behavior

The class should be pickled and be stored in the cache

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.44.0
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

facts_with_quotes.quote:
Application Crash: file_uploader kills streamlit when used in a page via st.navigation 1.47 and 1.48 at least

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi,

Platform is windows 11, recent python, streamlit version 1.47 and 1.48

I can't see this described in the issues list.

I just spend a couple of hours tracing a very strange problem with st.file_uploader. The problem affects files of any size, including 1kB and doesn't seem to cause run away memory usage in streamlit.

If I create a simple app with the following file_uploader everything works as expected, file is uploaded and the message is printed

```
  import streamlit as st
  
  st.write(st.__version__)
  
  uploads = st.file_uploader("Upload one or more files")
  
  if uploads is not None:
      st.write("uploads")

```
However, if I create an application like this. Then the upload proceeds for a few seconds and then the server process dies with no diagnostics.

app.py

```
import streamlit as st

pg = st.navigation([
    st.Page("Upload_Data.py", title="Upload data"),
])
pg.run()

```

Upload_Data.py

```
import streamlit as st

st.write(st.__version__)

uploads = st.file_uploader("Upload one or more files")

if uploads is not None:
    st.write("uploads")


```

If I replace the string with the python filename with a function, which does the same thing then the function works correctly.

Expected behaviour

Application doesn't crash when using file_uploader in pages loaded via st.navigation.

Thanks for your help and any pointers.

Mike

### Summary

Watch discuss Topic:
https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/after-upload-file-stays-in-ram/119453/2

Streamlit Version 1.49.1
Python Version 3.13.7

I searched for the issue on all known databases without success

I am facing the following issue with st.file_uploader:

When I am uploading a File about 600MB the RAM usage is after I selected the File about 660 MB.
At the moment I pressed the upload button the RAM usage increases up to 1800MB.
After the Upload is done, the RAM usage stays at 660MB.
If I close the browsertab it stays at 660MB, only when I close the streamlit instance the RAM gets free.

I tryed several solutions:

clear_on_submit=True
working with session state keys
gc.collect()
st.rerun()

The phenomenon is:
If I set the clear_on_submit=false and deactivate the st.rerun() I am able to delete the File in the Widget and only then the file gets deleted from the RAM.

I tested it with a simple Upload code with the same result in different browsers on 2 different PCs and different streamlit versions.

Actually I have no idea how to fix this, can somebody help?

summary.problem:
Add an option to fully disable sidebar rendering until authentication or page load is complete

Currently, Streamlit always renders the sidebar and multipage navigation menu before any backend logic runs.
This causes a brief flash (“flicker”) of the sidebar, even when developers try to hide it using CSS, st.set_page_config(initial_sidebar_state="collapsed"), or st.stop() during login checks.

Problem

When implementing authentication or loading processes (e.g., validating user credentials via an API), Streamlit renders the sidebar before the authentication state is known.
This behavior creates two key issues:

Security concern:
Unauthenticated users can briefly see and click sidebar navigation links before st.stop() halts the script, allowing them to access or attempt to load protected pages.
Even if no data is exposed, it creates a visible loophole and inconsistent behavior.

UX inconsistency:
The sidebar “flashes” for a fraction of a second during app load, even when the developer intends to display only a centered login screen or full-screen loading animation.
This leads to a jarring visual experience and makes professional deployments look less polished.

Why this matters

Many enterprise and production Streamlit apps use custom login systems, SSO integrations, or data validation APIs before showing any content.

In these cases, developers need full control over what renders before authentication completes.

There’s currently no reliable way to prevent the sidebar or multipage navigation from being rendered briefly.


Proposed solution

Add a configuration flag such as:
st.set_page_config(show_sidebar_on_load=False)

st.cache_data on class methods intermittently raises UnserializableReturnValueError

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:
    def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0):
        self.output = output
        self.value = value

"""
Helper module imported once by repro.py.
Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference
after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.

import streamlit as st
from repro_model import MyResult  # bound once at import time


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    import time
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return MyResult(output=f"result for {key}", value=42)

import importlib

summary.problem:
st.cache_data shares cache across st.Page pages for same-named functions with different source code

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.cache_data functions with the same name but different source code in different page files (loaded via st.navigation + st.Page) share the same cache. This is because st.Page executes all pages via exec() with
  __module__ == "__main__", and inspect.getsource() fails in that context. The fallback to func.__code__.co_code (bytecode) does not include string constants, so functions with identical structure but different inline strings (e.g., different SQL queries) produce the same cache key.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# main.py
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(page_title="Cache Bug Demo", layout="wide")
pg = st.navigation(
    {
        "Page A": [st.Page("page_a.py", title="Page A")],
        "Page B": [st.Page("page_b.py", title="Page B")],
    }
)
pg.run()
# page_a.py
import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_a", "columns": ["col_a1", "col_a2"]}


data = load_data()
st.write("Page A data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_a, Got:", data["source"])
# page_b.py
import streamlit as st


@st.cache_data(ttl=3600)
def load_data():
    return {"source": "page_b", "columns": ["col_b1", "col_b2"]}


data = load_data()
st.write("Page B data:", data)
st.write("Expected source: page_b, Got:", data["source"])
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Create the three files above (main.py, page_a.py, page_b.py)
2. Run streamlit run main.py
3. Open Page A — displays source: page_a (correct)
4. Navigate to Page B — displays source: page_a (wrong, should be page_b)
5. Clear cache and open Page B first — displays source: page_b (correct)
6. Navigate to Page A — displays source: page_b (wrong, should be page_a)

### Expected Behavior

Each page's load_data() should have an independent cache, since they are defined in different files with different source code. Navigating between pages should return each page's own data.

Whichever page is loaded first caches its result under the function key. When the other page calls its own load_data(), the cached result from the first page is returned, because both functions

summary.problem:
Updating selectbox selection that is saved in st.session_state needs to be clicked twice

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hello everyone. 

In my use case, I have a multipage application, with an st.selectbox on top of every subpage. The default value of those selectboxes is taken from st.session_state. The bug I have encountered now is that when I want to update the selectbox value I need to select the new value twice. An example

Selected option: 1
I select option 2.
Selected option: 1
I select option 2 again.
Selected option: 2

From then on the value is updated and working as expected. This behavior is 100% reproducible for me but only happening after I updated the selected option once i.e. directly after the start of the application it works fine and expected once. Afterward I need to double select the options.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
app.py:
import streamlit as st

def main():
    pg = st.navigation([st.Page("page1.py")])
    pg.run()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()


page1.py:
import streamlit as st


def page():
    if "selectedIndex" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state["selectedIndex"] = 0
    
    selectedIndex = st.selectbox(
        label="Select something:", 
        options=range(0, 5),
        index=st.session_state["selectedIndex"]
    )
    
    st.session_state["selectedIndex"] = selectedIndex
    
    st.write(f"You selected {selectedIndex}.")
    st.write(f"Session state {st.session_state["selectedIndex"]}.")


page()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start the application `streamlit run app.py`
2. Update the select box value to 3.
4. Select option 1.
6. Select option 1 again.

You can repeat steps 4-7 as often as you want; it will happen every time.

### Expected Behavior

1. Start the application `streamlit run app.py`
2. Update the select box value to 3.
3. The value is now correctly set as 3.
4. Select option 1.6. 
5. The value is now correctly set as 1.

### Current Behavior

No error messages.

1. Start the application `streamlit run app.py`
2. Update the select box value to 3.
3. The value is now correctly set as 3.
4. Select option 1.
5. The selected value will jump back to 3. The return value and session state value also don't update.
6. Select option

summary.problem:
Deleting a widget's session_state key leaves the frontend showing the stale value (backend/frontend divergence for one rerun)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Deleting a keyed widget's entry from `st.session_state` (e.g. `del st.session_state["foo"]` inside a callback) does not reset the widget, but can lead to an inconsistency between frontend and backend.

The Python side returns the widget's *default* value for that run, but the frontend keeps displaying the old value, so backend and frontend disagree.

On the **next** rerun the backend silently re-adopts the stale frontend value, so the deletion is effectively undone.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

text = st.text_input("Foo", value="default", key="foo")

st.write("widget returned:", repr(text))

def populate():
    st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"

def delete():
    del st.session_state["foo"]

st.button("Populate", on_click=populate)
st.button("Delete", on_click=delete)
st.button("Noop")

```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app.
2. Click **Populate** (callback sets `st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"`). The text input now shows `hello` and `widget returned: 'hello'`.
3. Click **Delete** (callback runs `del st.session_state["foo"]`).
4. Observe the text input on screen vs. the `widget returned:` line.
5. Click **Noop** (any interaction that triggers a plain rerun) and observe again.

### Expected Behavior

The widget value in the frontent and backend should be consistent. After deleting a widget's key in session state, it should presumably fall back to its default value.

### Current Behavior

- After clicking Delete, the backend returns `widget returned: "default''` , but the frontend widget still displays `"hello"`.
- After the next rerun (step 5), the backend re-adopts the stale frontend value, and both show `"hello"`.

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

summary.problem:
`setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`

### Summary

When a Components V2 component calls `setTriggerValue` during mount (inside the default function, rather than from a user event handler), values are silently lost if the component remounts because its `data` changed — even when an explicit `key` is passed, which keeps the element id stable.

Measured roughly a quarter loss: **5 of 21 values sent were never received by Python at all.** They are not late — a scan of the entire session log shows they never arrive in any subsequent run.

This is split out of #14710, where it surfaced during investigation. It is distinct from the two by-design mechanisms discussed there (`data` participating in element identity for unkeyed components, and trigger values resetting after each run).

**Update — measured root cause.** A frontend race in `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive`: it destroys the synthetic trigger-aggregator widget state while that state is still awaiting its batched flush, so the app reruns with no trigger at all. Not a backend discard. Measured on a production build with the repro below: 10/85 values lost unpatched vs 0/85 patched, and with instrumentation, 14/14 losses correlated exactly with the destroying call. Mechanism and open question under Additional Information.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

comp = st.components.v2.component(
    "repro.mount_trigger",
    js="""
    export default function (component) {
        const v = "val" + component.data.nonce;
        console.log("SEND " + v);
        component.setTriggerValue("v", v);
    }
    """,
)

if "clicks" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.clicks = 0
if st.button("bump"):
    st.session_state.clicks += 1

nonce = f"c{st.session_state.clicks}"
result = comp(data={"nonce": nonce}, key="stable_key")

received = result.get("v")
st.write(f"data nonce {nonce} -> received {received!r}")
print(f"nonce={nonce} received={received!r}", flush=True)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and open the browser console.
2. Click **bump** ~20 times, letting the app settle between clicks. Each click changes `data`, so the component remounts and sends one value.
3. Compare the `SEND val…` lines in the console against the `received=…` lines in the terminal.
4. Roughly one in four sent values never appears on the Python side.

summary.problem:
`setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`

### Summary

When a Components V2 component calls `setTriggerValue` during mount (inside the default function, rather than from a user event handler), values are silently lost if the component remounts because its `data` changed — even when an explicit `key` is passed, which keeps the element id stable.

Measured roughly a quarter loss: **5 of 21 values sent were never received by Python at all.** They are not late — a scan of the entire session log shows they never arrive in any subsequent run.

This is split out of #14710, where it surfaced during investigation. It is distinct from the two by-design mechanisms discussed there (`data` participating in element identity for unkeyed components, and trigger values resetting after each run).

**Update — measured root cause.** A frontend race in `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive`: it destroys the synthetic trigger-aggregator widget state while that state is still awaiting its batched flush, so the app reruns with no trigger at all. Not a backend discard. Measured on a production build with the repro below: 10/85 values lost unpatched vs 0/85 patched, and with instrumentation, 14/14 losses correlated exactly with the destroying call. Mechanism and open question under Additional Information.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

comp = st.components.v2.component(
    "repro.mount_trigger",
    js="""
    export default function (component) {
        const v = "val" + component.data.nonce;
        console.log("SEND " + v);
        component.setTriggerValue("v", v);
    }
    """,
)

if "clicks" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.clicks = 0
if st.button("bump"):
    st.session_state.clicks += 1

nonce = f"c{st.session_state.clicks}"
result = comp(data={"nonce": nonce}, key="stable_key")

received = result.get("v")
st.write(f"data nonce {nonce} -> received {received!r}")
print(f"nonce={nonce} received={received!r}", flush=True)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and open the browser console.
2. Click **bump** ~20 times, letting the app settle between clicks. Each click changes `data`, so the component remounts and sends one value.
3. Compare the `SEND val…` lines in the console against the `received=…` lines in the terminal.
4. Roughly one in four sent values never appears on the Python side.

BUG: wrong value returned by backend vs frontend, when a widget is rendered after a previous page run set a default value in session state

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

If a default value is set in session state on one page run, and then subsequently a widget is rendered with a corresponding `key`, then the default value is not picked up properly and the frontend and backend show different values for that widget.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# Sets default on first page run
st.session_state.setdefault("foo", 100.0)

if st.toggle("Show"):
    foo = st.number_input("Foo", key="foo")  # Shows 0.00
    st.write("You entered:", foo)  # Shows 100.0
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1.Turn on the  toggle
2. Compare the value in the widget vs the value printed underneath

### Expected Behavior

The value in the widget should match the number reported underneath.

### Current Behavior

The input widget displays `0.00`, but the backend reports `You entered: 100`.

If `r` is pressed to trigger a re-run, then the frontend updates to display `0.0` and the default value is lost.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

This bug is problematic for more complex pages, where widgets may need to be "loaded" or "reset" programmatically, and some widgets may be conditionally hidden depending on a toggle or checkbox.

summary.problem:
Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.

### Summary

summary.problem:
Support multiple sidebars and put the page list into a separated sidebar

### Problem

It's easy to get overcrowded when sharing a single sidebar.

I need three separated sidebars for:

1. page tools (original sidebar)
2. a long list for multiple apps/pages
3. a shared/public config panel across pages (e.g. editing `session_state`, showing ENV variables...)

### Solution

The UI may look like this (three icons):

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

Pseudo code in `app.py` (main page):

```py
import streamlit as st

def provide_page_list():
    ...
    
# name, icon_image, callback_function
st.add_left_bar_item("page", "page.png", provide_page_list)


def shared_panel():
    ...
    return ["pages/about.py", "pages/monitor.py",  ...]

# name, icon_image, callback_function
st.add_right_bar_item("tool", "tool.png", shared_panel)
```

A `right_bar_item` is also a sidebar, but it shows at the right side.

The `add_left_bar_item` / `add_right_bar_item` will be shared across pages, since the traditional sidebar is used for current page only.

You can open one left sidebar and one right sidebar at the same time, but you can only open one sidebar for each side (it means that when you open the second left sidebar, it will close the first one).

summary.problem:
Session State convenience function for initialization

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

It'd be nice for Session State to have a convenience method for initializing it.

### Why?

Many apps have boilerplate code:
```python
if "my_key" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.my_key = "default_value"
```
If there are multiple keys, you might shortcut the logical test to check for one and initialize all others:
```python
if "A" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.A = "A"
    st.session_state.B = "B"
    st.session_state.C = "C"
```
If any of the keys were associated to a widget and the widget wasn't continuously rendered, you could have a situation will all keys initialized on session start, but maybe "B" or "C" got deleted later. Thus, to be really thorough, you'd need:

```python
session_init = {"A":"A", "B":"B", "C":"C"}
for key, value in session_init.items():
    st.session_state[key] = value
```

It might be nice to have a convenience function to handle the latter:

```python
st.session_state.from_dict({"A":"A", "B":"B", "C":"C"})
```

A parameter could be used to distinguish between initializing (set if not exists), updating (dictionary merge), or full replacement (delete other keys).


### How?

Similar to how `st.query_params` is a dict-like interface with a few extra functions, `st.session_state` could get a convenience function or two.

### Additional Context

summary.problem:
st.radio label alignment and label_visibility issues in the latest versions

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The st.radio widget has two unexpected behaviors in the latest versions of Streamlit:

The label is centered instead of left-aligned, which is inconsistent with previous versions.
The label_visibility option 'collapsed' does not work as expected, and the label remains visible.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# Store the initial value of widgets in session state
if "visibility" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.visibility = "visible"
    st.session_state.disabled = False
    st.session_state.horizontal = False

col1, col2 = st.columns(2)

with col1:
    st.checkbox("Disable radio widget", key="disabled")
    st.checkbox("Orient radio options horizontally", key="horizontal")

with col2:
    st.radio(
        "Set label visibility 👇",
        ["visible", "hidden", "collapsed"],
        key="visibility",
        label_visibility=st.session_state.visibility,
        disabled=st.session_state.disabled,
        horizontal=st.session_state.horizontal,
    )
```


### Steps To Reproduce

please play with the options of the above snippet, and inspect label

### Expected Behavior

The label of the st.radio widget should be left-aligned, consistent with previous versions.
When label_visibility='collapsed' is set, the label should not be visible.

### Current Behavior

The label is centered.
Setting label_visibility='collapsed' does not hide the label; it remains visible.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.41.1
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:


### Additional Information

AxiosError: timeout exceeded - Streamlit file uploader

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`AxiosError: timeout exceeded` happens when uploading a CSV file to the file uploader widget. This error happens in my app hosted on both localhost and the Streamlit community cloud. It happens when I use a different browser and different CSV files too. Doesn't work when I disabled XsrfProtection in `config.toml` either. I tried disabling like this:
``
[server]
enableXsrfProtection = false
``

I tried making a new app from scratch with a new Python environment (3.11), that only has one Streamlit file uploader, but the same error happened. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.file_uploader("Upload a file")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start the app on localhost 
2. Upload a csv file, for example, the one attached here
[case2lignin.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18127875/case2lignin.csv)


### Expected Behavior

 The csv file is successfully uploaded. 

### Current Behavior

`AxiosError: timeout exceeded` happens and the file is not uploaded. 

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:  1.41.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: MacOS Sequoia 15.1
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

### Summary

Hello,

Currently, Streamlit stores the entirety of uploaded files in memory. This limits upload size to available RAM of the machine.

I managed to implement chunked multipart uploads straight to disk, allowing for arbitrary upload sizes.
However my knowledge of Streamlit's inner workings is quite limited and I can't find an elegant solution worthy of a PR.
Hence I wanted to share with you parts of my solution, in the hope of someone picking it up and implementing it properly.

---

I started by subclassing `UploadFileRequestHandler` (`streamlit/web/server/upload_file_request_handler.py`), which handles the file upload:
1. By decorating it with `@tornado.web.stream_request_body`, we can can define a `data_received(self, chunk)` method to receive chunked data.
2. Using the package [`python-multipart`](https://pypi.org/project/python-multipart/), we can create a parser in the `prepare()` method, and feed it data in the previously mentionned `data_received(self, chunk)`.
3. `python-multipart` then gives us access to a `File` instance through an `on_file()` method that we define on the class.

This is where it got very hacky and custom for me, modifying `UploadedFile`, `UploadedFileRec` etc., and where I believe an expert view would be welcomed.

Here is the full code:

        self.file_id = self.path_kwargs['file_id']

`st.cache_data` can't replay `st.status.update()` effect

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The `.update()` call of status container can't be replayed inside a cached function with `st.cache_data`, resulting in the status stuck with the init content.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st
@st.cache_data
def show_data():
    with st.status("Downloading data...", expanded=True) as status:
        st.write("Searching for data...")
        time.sleep(2)
        st.write("Found URL.")
        time.sleep(1)
        st.write("Downloading data...")
        time.sleep(1)
        status.update(
            label="Download complete!", state="complete", expanded=False
        )

show_data()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

use status container inside a cached function with st.cache_data, then call status.update

### Expected Behavior

When reruning the cached function, the status container should replay the "Download complete!" update after the st.write effects.

### Current Behavior

the status container replays only the st.write effects, but stuck in "Downloading data..." because the last update is not replayed:

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The `.update()` call of status container can't be replayed inside a cached function with `st.cache_data`, resulting in the status stuck with the init content.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st
@st.cache_data
def show_data():
    with st.status("Downloading data...", expanded=True) as status:
        st.write("Searching for data...")
        time.sleep(2)
        st.write("Found URL.")
        time.sleep(1)
        st.write("Downloading data...")
        time.sleep(1)
        status.update(
            label="Download complete!", state="complete", expanded=False
        )

show_data()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

use status container inside a cached function with st.cache_data, then call status.update

### Expected Behavior

When reruning the cached function, the status container should replay the "Download complete!" update after the st.write effects.

### Current Behavior

the status container replays only the st.write effects, but stuck in "Downloading data..." because the last update is not replayed:
[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Browser: Chrome

summary.problem:
Make sections in navigation menu collapsable

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

A project with several/many sections and pages shows at start and all the time every entity.
To minimize that view for the user and to focus, it should be possible to collapse sections (with its pages below). 

### Why?

The app should be able to leave away, and give the user the ability to do so by itself, what is not immediately necessary or important

### How?

add an optional parameter for sections in pages: collapse(true/false) which declares the inital state on load

behaviour:
1. if the parameter itself is given, show an icon after the header title
2. the icon depends on the value:
    1. false: ▲
    2. true: ▼

### Additional Context

take a look on the menu on the left on https://docs.streamlit.io/

summary.problem:
Unexpected Page Refresh and Lost Selection in Streamlit 1.24.0 when using image_select

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I encountered an issue with Streamlit version 1.24.0 where the page would refresh entirely, causing the loss of the selected item when using the image_select function. However, the problem was not present in Streamlit version 1.22.0. As a workaround, I am currently using Streamlit 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.

Steps to Reproduce:

Upgrade Streamlit to version 1.24.0.
Implement an app that includes the image_select function.
Run the app and observe the behavior when using image_select to select an item.
Notice that upon selection, the entire page refreshes, leading to the loss of the selected item.
Expected Behavior:
When using image_select, the selection should be retained without causing the page to refresh entirely (session states should keep the current selection active)

Actual Behavior:
In Streamlit version 1.24.0, the page refreshes entirely, resulting in the loss of the selected item.

Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.24.0
Not Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.22.0
Additional Notes:

The issue specifically affects Streamlit version 1.24.0, but it was not present in version 1.22.0.
The unexpected page refresh and lost selection occur specifically when using the image_select function.
As a temporary workaround, I am using Streamlit version 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.
This behavior significantly impacts user experience, as it prevents the proper selection of items within the app.
Environment:

Operating System: [Win 11]
Python version: [3.10]
Streamlit version: 1.24.0
This issue is submitted to report the unexpected page refresh and lost selection problem that occurs when using the image_select function in Streamlit version 1.24.0. The problem was not observed in Streamlit version 1.22.0, and for the time being, I am using that version as a workaround. It would be helpful to investigate and address this behavior to ensure the smooth functioning of applications using image_select.

summary.problem:
Unexpected Page Refresh and Lost Selection in Streamlit 1.24.0 when using image_select

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I encountered an issue with Streamlit version 1.24.0 where the page would refresh entirely, causing the loss of the selected item when using the image_select function. However, the problem was not present in Streamlit version 1.22.0. As a workaround, I am currently using Streamlit 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.

Steps to Reproduce:

Upgrade Streamlit to version 1.24.0.
Implement an app that includes the image_select function.
Run the app and observe the behavior when using image_select to select an item.
Notice that upon selection, the entire page refreshes, leading to the loss of the selected item.
Expected Behavior:
When using image_select, the selection should be retained without causing the page to refresh entirely (session states should keep the current selection active)

Actual Behavior:
In Streamlit version 1.24.0, the page refreshes entirely, resulting in the loss of the selected item.

Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.24.0
Not Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.22.0
Additional Notes:

The issue specifically affects Streamlit version 1.24.0, but it was not present in version 1.22.0.
The unexpected page refresh and lost selection occur specifically when using the image_select function.
As a temporary workaround, I am using Streamlit version 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.
This behavior significantly impacts user experience, as it prevents the proper selection of items within the app.
Environment:

Operating System: [Win 11]
Python version: [3.10]
Streamlit version: 1.24.0
This issue is submitted to report the unexpected page refresh and lost selection problem that occurs when using the image_select function in Streamlit version 1.24.0. The problem was not observed in Streamlit version 1.22.0, and for the time being, I am using that version as a workaround. It would be helpful to investigate and address this behavior to ensure the smooth functioning of applications using image_select.

summary.problem:
Support multiple sidebars and put the page list into a separated sidebar

### Problem

It's easy to get overcrowded when sharing a single sidebar.

I need three separated sidebars for:

1. page tools (original sidebar)
2. a long list for multiple apps/pages
3. a shared/public config panel across pages (e.g. editing `session_state`, showing ENV variables...)

### Solution

The UI may look like this (three icons):

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

Pseudo code in `app.py` (main page):

```py
import streamlit as st

def provide_page_list():
    ...
    
# name, icon_image, callback_function
st.add_left_bar_item("page", "page.png", provide_page_list)


def shared_panel():
    ...
    return ["pages/about.py", "pages/monitor.py",  ...]

# name, icon_image, callback_function
st.add_right_bar_item("tool", "tool.png", shared_panel)
```

A `right_bar_item` is also a sidebar, but it shows at the right side.

The `add_left_bar_item` / `add_right_bar_item` will be shared across pages, since the traditional sidebar is used for current page only.

You can open one left sidebar and one right sidebar at the same time, but you can only open one sidebar for each side (it means that when you open the second left sidebar, it will close the first one).

Trigger for user leaving the page

I have a dynamically generated forms for user to edit different objects. To keep track of what's happening - part of info is saved to session state (like, validation results to be displayed on next script rerun). **MVP:** It would be great to have some kind of `trap`, which triggers, if it is NOT reached on next rerun (i.e. run action, if it's not disarmed during the run). This would allow to clear up session_state leftovers cleanly.

summary.problem:
Session State convenience function for initialization

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

It'd be nice for Session State to have a convenience method for initializing it.

### Why?

Many apps have boilerplate code:
```python
if "my_key" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.my_key = "default_value"
```
If there are multiple keys, you might shortcut the logical test to check for one and initialize all others:
```python
if "A" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.A = "A"
    st.session_state.B = "B"
    st.session_state.C = "C"
```
If any of the keys were associated to a widget and the widget wasn't continuously rendered, you could have a situation will all keys initialized on session start, but maybe "B" or "C" got deleted later. Thus, to be really thorough, you'd need:

```python
session_init = {"A":"A", "B":"B", "C":"C"}
for key, value in session_init.items():
    st.session_state[key] = value
```

It might be nice to have a convenience function to handle the latter:

```python
st.session_state.from_dict({"A":"A", "B":"B", "C":"C"})
```

A parameter could be used to distinguish between initializing (set if not exists), updating (dictionary merge), or full replacement (delete other keys).


### How?

Similar to how `st.query_params` is a dict-like interface with a few extra functions, `st.session_state` could get a convenience function or two.

### Additional Context

summary.problem:
st.radio label alignment and label_visibility issues in the latest versions

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The st.radio widget has two unexpected behaviors in the latest versions of Streamlit:

The label is centered instead of left-aligned, which is inconsistent with previous versions.
The label_visibility option 'collapsed' does not work as expected, and the label remains visible.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# Store the initial value of widgets in session state
if "visibility" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.visibility = "visible"
    st.session_state.disabled = False
    st.session_state.horizontal = False

col1, col2 = st.columns(2)

with col1:
    st.checkbox("Disable radio widget", key="disabled")
    st.checkbox("Orient radio options horizontally", key="horizontal")

with col2:
    st.radio(
        "Set label visibility 👇",
        ["visible", "hidden", "collapsed"],
        key="visibility",
        label_visibility=st.session_state.visibility,
        disabled=st.session_state.disabled,
        horizontal=st.session_state.horizontal,
    )
```


### Steps To Reproduce

please play with the options of the above snippet, and inspect label

### Expected Behavior

The label of the st.radio widget should be left-aligned, consistent with previous versions.
When label_visibility='collapsed' is set, the label should not be visible.

### Current Behavior

The label is centered.
Setting label_visibility='collapsed' does not hide the label; it remains visible.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.41.1
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

facts_with_quotes.quote:
AxiosError: timeout exceeded - Streamlit file uploader

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`AxiosError: timeout exceeded` happens when uploading a CSV file to the file uploader widget. This error happens in my app hosted on both localhost and the Streamlit community cloud. It happens when I use a different browser and different CSV files too. Doesn't work when I disabled XsrfProtection in `config.toml` either. I tried disabling like this:
``
[server]
enableXsrfProtection = false
``

I tried making a new app from scratch with a new Python environment (3.11), that only has one Streamlit file uploader, but the same error happened. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.file_uploader("Upload a file")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start the app on localhost 
2. Upload a csv file, for example, the one attached here
[case2lignin.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18127875/case2lignin.csv)


### Expected Behavior

 The csv file is successfully uploaded. 

### Current Behavior

`AxiosError: timeout exceeded` happens and the file is not uploaded. 

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:  1.41.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: MacOS Sequoia 15.1
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

summary.problem:
Code snippet to upload files to disk in chunks rather than in memory

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Hello,

Currently, Streamlit stores the entirety of uploaded files in memory. This limits upload size to available RAM of the machine.

I managed to implement chunked multipart uploads straight to disk, allowing for arbitrary upload sizes.
However my knowledge of Streamlit's inner workings is quite limited and I can't find an elegant solution worthy of a PR.
Hence I wanted to share with you parts of my solution, in the hope of someone picking it up and implementing it properly.

---

I started by subclassing `UploadFileRequestHandler` (`streamlit/web/server/upload_file_request_handler.py`), which handles the file upload:
1. By decorating it with `@tornado.web.stream_request_body`, we can can define a `data_received(self, chunk)` method to receive chunked data.
2. Using the package [`python-multipart`](https://pypi.org/project/python-multipart/), we can create a parser in the `prepare()` method, and feed it data in the previously mentionned `data_received(self, chunk)`.
3. `python-multipart` then gives us access to a `File` instance through an `on_file()` method that we define on the class.

This is where it got very hacky and custom for me, modifying `UploadedFile`, `UploadedFileRec` etc., and where I believe an expert view would be welcomed.

Here is the full code:

        self.file_id = self.path_kwargs['file_id']
        self.bytes_received = 0

summary.problem:
Code snippet to upload files to disk in chunks rather than in memory

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Hello,

Currently, Streamlit stores the entirety of uploaded files in memory. This limits upload size to available RAM of the machine.

I managed to implement chunked multipart uploads straight to disk, allowing for arbitrary upload sizes.
However my knowledge of Streamlit's inner workings is quite limited and I can't find an elegant solution worthy of a PR.
Hence I wanted to share with you parts of my solution, in the hope of someone picking it up and implementing it properly.

---

I started by subclassing `UploadFileRequestHandler` (`streamlit/web/server/upload_file_request_handler.py`), which handles the file upload:
1. By decorating it with `@tornado.web.stream_request_body`, we can can define a `data_received(self, chunk)` method to receive chunked data.
2. Using the package [`python-multipart`](https://pypi.org/project/python-multipart/), we can create a parser in the `prepare()` method, and feed it data in the previously mentionned `data_received(self, chunk)`.
3. `python-multipart` then gives us access to a `File` instance through an `on_file()` method that we define on the class.

This is where it got very hacky and custom for me, modifying `UploadedFile`, `UploadedFileRec` etc., and where I believe an expert view would be welcomed.

Here is the full code:

        self.file_id = self.path_kwargs['file_id']
        self.bytes_received = 0

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Can we have a button / icon to the top right of the file uploader widget? 

### Why?

In case you want to upload a fresh set of (multiple) files, you need to first delete the earlier list of (multiple) files attached to the uploader widget. It becomes impractical to individually delete the attached files.

### How?

Suggestion: Have a delete icon (like with st.data_editor) to do this - ref encircled 'x' in the following pix. This icon, when pressed, will clear all files attached to the widget at one go.

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.

### Summary

Browser sessions allow developers to track browser status in streamlit, so that they can implement features like authentication, persistent draft or shopping cart, which require the ability to keep user state after refreshing or reopen browsers.

### Why?

The current streamlit session will lost state if users refresh or reopen their browser. And the effort of providing a API to write cookies has been pending for years. I think provide a dedicated API to track browser session would be cleaner and easier to implement.  
With this API developers don't need to know how it works, it can be based on cookie or local storage or anything else. And developers can use it with singleton pattern to keep state for browser to persist whatever they want in streamlit.

### How?

* `st.get_browser_session(gdpr_consent=False)`, which will set a unique session id in browser if it doesn't exist, and return it.
If `gdpr_consent` is set to True, a window will pop up to ask for user's consent before setting the session id.
* `st.clean_browser_session()`, which will remove the session id from browser.
