`st.cache_data` can't replay `st.status.update()` effect

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The `.update()` call of status container can't be replayed inside a cached function with `st.cache_data`, resulting in the status stuck with the init content.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st
@st.cache_data
def show_data():
    with st.status("Downloading data...", expanded=True) as status:
        st.write("Searching for data...")
        time.sleep(2)
        st.write("Found URL.")
        time.sleep(1)
        st.write("Downloading data...")
        time.sleep(1)
        status.update(
            label="Download complete!", state="complete", expanded=False
        )

show_data()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

use status container inside a cached function with st.cache_data, then call status.update

### Expected Behavior

When reruning the cached function, the status container should replay the "Download complete!" update after the st.write effects.

### Current Behavior

the status container replays only the st.write effects, but stuck in "Downloading data..." because the last update is not replayed:
[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.40.1
- Python version: 3.12

- Browser: Chrome

summary.problem:
`st.cache_data` can't replay `st.status.update()` effect

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The `.update()` call of status container can't be replayed inside a cached function with `st.cache_data`, resulting in the status stuck with the init content.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st
@st.cache_data
def show_data():
    with st.status("Downloading data...", expanded=True) as status:
        st.write("Searching for data...")
        time.sleep(2)
        st.write("Found URL.")
        time.sleep(1)
        st.write("Downloading data...")
        time.sleep(1)
        status.update(
            label="Download complete!", state="complete", expanded=False
        )

show_data()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

use status container inside a cached function with st.cache_data, then call status.update

### Expected Behavior

When reruning the cached function, the status container should replay the "Download complete!" update after the st.write effects.

### Current Behavior

the status container replays only the st.write effects, but stuck in "Downloading data..." because the last update is not replayed:
[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.40.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Windows 10
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

summary.problem:
Sidebar Shakes When Bookmarks Are Enabled

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

My screen resolution is 1920 x 1080. The problem occurs when I enable bookmarks on Chrome version 130.0.6723.59 (64-bit), and the sidebar in my Streamlit app starts shaking. Could this be a bug?

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

with st.sidebar:
    st.image('1024_image.jpg')
    st.page_link('app.py', label='main_page')
    st.page_link('pages/test.py', label='test_page')
    st.divider()

    sb1 = st.selectbox('1st sb', ['1', '2', '3'], index=None)
    if sb1:
        sb2 = st.selectbox('2nd sb', ['4', '5', '6'], index=None)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the code https://github.com/mrseongminkim/streamlit-report/tree/main
2. Open it with Chrome 130.0.6723.59 (64-bit)
3. Enable bookmarks

### Expected Behavior

Not shaking sidebar

### Current Behavior

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.39.0
- Python version: Python 3.10.13
- Operating System: Windows 10
- Browser: Chrome 130.0.6723.59 (64-bit)


### Additional Information

I also opened a post in https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/sidebar-shakes-when-bookmarks-are-enabled/83784/1
Thank you!

summary.problem:
Make sections in navigation menu collapsable

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

A project with several/many sections and pages shows at start and all the time every entity.
To minimize that view for the user and to focus, it should be possible to collapse sections (with its pages below). 

### Why?

The app should be able to leave away, and give the user the ability to do so by itself, what is not immediately necessary or important

### How?

add an optional parameter for sections in pages: collapse(true/false) which declares the inital state on load

behaviour:
1. if the parameter itself is given, show an icon after the header title
2. the icon depends on the value:
    1. false: ▲
    2. true: ▼

### Additional Context

take a look on the menu on the left on https://docs.streamlit.io/
summary.rationale: محدودیت: این خروجی با سیاست آزمایشی قطعی ساخته شده و کیفیت مدل زبانی را اثبات نمی‌کند. نسخه و منبع باید توسط بازبین بررسی شوند.
